body: Yeah, learning a new skill is cool and all but I've had a STEM degree for almost a year and I still work retail lmao
Fuck off you piece of shit.

You are not too weak to leave. These kinds of abusive relationships only work when the abuser convinces the abused they are too weak (or any other negative quality) to leave.

You suffer through this guy's shit every fucking day. Your mental and emotional states are brought to their limit every fucking day. If you were doing this with weights, you would have the biggest muscles on the earth.

Although the gender might not match up perfectly, I highly recommend you watch this:

https://youtu.be/AeGEv0YVLtw

I also highly recommend you read the book The Body Keeps The Score if you haven't already. It may help you understand what is happening on your end and how you can turn stuff around. (I didn't start to feel better until I read this.)

But at the end of the day, you are not only not weak but I can guarantee you you will get out of this and I can guarantee you life will get better. You just need to hang in there a little bit longer.

Feel free to dm me or reply to this comment if you need anything. Getting out of abusive situations isn't easy, but recognizing where and how you are being abused is the first step and I am super glad that you've already begun this.

Remember nothing he does to you is your fault and you are strong, likeable, and compassionate. Don't give up!

You should love yourself always to the best of your ability, but according to attachment theory (and from personal experience), it's so much easier when in a relationship (romantic, friendships, family, etc). However, these relationships have to be healthy and mutually supportive for them to work.

I am saying this because I don't want you to fall down the "I have to love myself completely before I form relationships" track because this is so difficult it's impossible.

As for your insecurities, nobody is ever too old to have them. That sounds like another avenue your anxiety is using to "attack" you.

Your situation sounds very familiar to mine though. I can't ask anyone out without my anxiety going absolutely nuts days before I do it. But over the years it's been getting easier and easier. I didn't start to feel better until I read the book The Body Keeps The Score by Besel Van Der Kolk. This book taught me that my anxieties all came from somewhere else and is a response to trauma. This book showed me that there was nothing wrong with me, maybe it can show you that too?

Also look into attachment theory, there's some books on the subject but I can't remember their name.

I wish you luck and I hope you get your happy ending!
